hook.line: Hernando's favourite subject is what has changed on the block and what hasn't. Four little words carry the whole conversation: already, still, not any more and not yet.
hook.es: Ya no hay radio en el café.
hook.en: There's no radio in the café any more.

examples.en: I don't live in Toronto any more.
Hernando still comes to the café.

Have you eaten yet?
Not yet.
Do you still live in Medellín? (to a friend)

rule:
Four time words, all about then and now:
*ya*: already: *Vale ya llegó*.
*todavía*: still: *Todavía tengo la foto*.
*ya no*: not any more: *Ya no vivo en Toronto*.
*todavía no*: not yet: *Todavía no*.

They usually sit before the verb. English wraps not ... any more around the verb; Spanish keeps *ya no* together in front of it.

With *ya*, Spanish uses the plain past where English says has or have: *¿Ya comiste?* is have you eaten yet?
smallPrint: *Ya* and *todavía* are time adverbs. Later you'll pair *todavía no* with another past form for things that haven't happened yet.

options: I don't live in Toronto any more.
I still live in Toronto.
I don't live in Toronto yet.
I already have the photo.
I still have the photo.
I don't have the photo any more.
I already bought the bread.
I don't buy bread any more.
I haven't bought the bread yet.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *___ vivo en Toronto.* (*Ya no* or *Todavía no*) I don't live in Toronto any more.
yourTurn.why: Not any more is *ya no*; *todavía no* is not yet.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *___ tengo la foto.* (*Ya* or *Todavía*) I still have the photo.
Ask a friend: Have you eaten yet?
Hernando still comes to the café.

yourTurn.why: *Ya* with the plain past *llegó*; no has in Spanish.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it's changed: *Tengo carro.* (I don't have a car any more.)
yourTurn.why: *Ya no* goes together, right before the verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it hasn't happened yet: *Ya compré el pan.*
yourTurn.why: Not yet is *todavía no*, before the verb.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Todavía no* is not yet; for not any more, Spanish says *ya no*.
Keep *ya no* together in front of the verb, not split around it.

personal: Write one thing you don't do any more (*ya no*), one thing you still do (*todavía*) and one thing you haven't done yet (*todavía no*).
